Cao Z.role: Last author of the 2026 study on how the pollutant EDPrB causes kidney disease through mTOR.
Cao Z.sub: Heilongjiang Key Laboratory for Laboratory Animals and Comparative Medicine · Northeast Agricultural University, Harbin, China
story: In mice and in human kidney cells grown in a dish, the pollutant EDPrB built up in the kidney and led to chronic kidney disease. The damage ran through overactive mTOR, which switched down autophagy (the cell's clean-up system) and set off inflammation and scar tissue. Giving the mice rapamycin reversed the harm, which pointed to mTOR activation as the first step in the chain. Cao is the last of five authors, and PubMed lists the affiliation as the Heilongjiang laboratory named above.

highlights.MIAO2026: Last of five authors on the mouse and cell study linking EDPrB exposure to mTOR-driven kidney disease.

Cao Z.lab_name: Heilongjiang Key Laboratory for Laboratory Animals and Comparative Medicine, College of Veterinary Medicine, Northeast Agricultural University (Harbin, China)

Miao C.role: First author of the 2026 study on how the pollutant EDPrB causes kidney disease through mTOR.
Miao C.sub: Heilongjiang Key Laboratory for Laboratory Animals and Comparative Medicine · Northeast Agricultural University, Harbin, China
story: In mice and in human kidney cells grown in a dish, the pollutant EDPrB built up in the kidney and led to chronic kidney disease. Mossmann D.role: First author of a 2018 review on how mTOR signalling and cell metabolism shape each other in cancer.
story: This is a review, so it gathers earlier work and does not report new experiments. It describes how mTOR signalling and cell metabolism depend on each other in cancer. Mossmann is the first of three authors, and PubMed lists the Biozentrum at the University of Basel.

highlights.MOS2018: First of three authors on the review of mTOR signalling and metabolism in cancer.

Stasyk T.role: Middle-listed co-author of two Atlas studies, on a kidney disease mechanism and on a lysosomal amino acid sensor.
Stasyk T.sub: Institute of Cell Biology, Biocenter · Medical University of Innsbruck, Austria
story: In a 2020 study using cells and mice, mTORC1 was shown to act on a protein called TFEB in a different way than on its other targets, and this route drives the kidney problems in Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome. A 2015 study found that SLC38A9, a protein in the lysosome membrane, is part of the machinery that senses amino acids for mTORC1.
Stasyk is a middle author on both papers. PubMed lists the cell biology group in Innsbruck, Austria, on each of them.

highlights.NAP2020: Middle author on the paper linking a TFEB-specific mTORC1 route to Birt-Hogg-Dube kidney disease.
highlights.REB2015: Middle author on the paper identifying SLC38A9 as part of the lysosomal amino acid sensing machinery.

Stasyk T.lab_name: Institute of Cell Biology, Biocenter, Medical University of Innsbruck (Innsbruck, Austria)

Nath P.role: First author of a 2026 mouse study of the mTOR inhibitor everolimus in head and neck cancer.
Nath P.sub: Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery · Louisiana State University Health, Shreveport, USA
story: In mouse models of TP53-mutant head and neck cancer, a tumour type that often escapes the immune system, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus slowed tumour growth. It brought more killer T cells and dendritic cells into the tumour, reduced regulatory T cells, and lowered PD-1 and PD-L1 levels, which restored T-cell activity. Nath is the first of nine authors, and PubMed lists the otolaryngology department at LSU Health Shreveport.

highlights.NAT2026: First of nine authors on the mouse study of everolimus reshaping the immune environment of TP53-mutant head and neck tumours.

Nath P.lab_name: Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Louisiana State University Health Shreveport (Shreveport, Louisiana, USA)

Nazio F.role: First author of a 2013 study on how mTOR holds back autophagy by controlling ULK1.
Nazio F.sub: Dulbecco Telethon Institute, Department of Biology · University of Rome Tor Vergata, Italy
story: This cell-based study showed that when mTOR is active, it blocks a protein called AMBRA1 by phosphorylation. When autophagy starts, AMBRA1 loses that phosphate and, together with the enzyme TRAF6, adds ubiquitin chains to ULK1, which makes ULK1 more stable and active. Nazio is the first of eleven authors, and PubMed lists the Dulbecco Telethon Institute in Rome.

highlights.NAZ2013: First of eleven authors on the study of the mTOR, AMBRA1, TRAF6 and ULK1 route that controls autophagy.

Nazio F.lab_name: Dulbecco Telethon Institute at the Department of Biology, University of Rome Tor Vergata (Rome, Italy)

Nazemi M.role: First author of a 2026 study on collagen I, amino acid uptake and mTORC1 in cancer cells.
Nazemi M.sub: School of Biosciences · University of Sheffield, United Kingdom
story: The study found that collagen I, a protein that is common around tumours, switches on mTORC1 through an integrin receptor and moves the amino acid transporter LAT1-4F2hc to the cell membrane. This keeps cancer cells supplied with essential amino acids and alive where nutrients are scarce. The transporter was also higher in basal-like breast and pancreatic tumours, where it tracked with poor outcomes. Nazemi is the first of six authors, and PubMed lists the University of Sheffield.

highlights.NAZ2026: First of six authors on the study of collagen I driving amino acid import and mTORC1 activity in cancer cells.

Nazemi M.lab_name: School of Biosciences, University of Sheffield (Sheffield, United Kingdom)

Brohée L.role: Middle-listed co-author of two Atlas studies, on G3BP proteins and the TSC complex and on malonyl-CoA as an mTORC1 inhibitor.
Brohée L.sub: Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing · Cologne, Germany
story: A 2021 study found that G3BP1 and G3BP2, proteins best known from stress granules, also hold the TSC complex on the lysosome. Without them, mTORC1 reacts too strongly to amino acids and insulin. A 2023 study showed that malonyl-CoA, a molecule made during fatty acid synthesis, binds the catalytic pocket of mTOR and blocks it, linking fat production to mTORC1 activity.
Brohee is a middle author on the 2021 paper and the second author on the 2023 paper. PubMed lists the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing in Cologne on both.

highlights.PRE2021: Middle author on the paper showing that G3BPs tether the TSC complex to lysosomes and restrain mTORC1.
highlights.NIC2023: Second of fourteen authors on the paper identifying malonyl-CoA as an ATP-competitive mTORC1 inhibitor.

Brohée L.lab_name: Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing (Cologne, Germany)

Figlia G.role: Middle-listed co-author of two Atlas studies, on G3BP proteins and the TSC complex and on malonyl-CoA as an mTORC1 inhibitor.
Figlia G.sub: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) · Heidelberg, Germany
story: A 2021 study found that G3BP1 and G3BP2, proteins best known from stress granules, also hold the TSC complex on the lysosome. Without them, mTORC1 reacts too strongly to amino acids and insulin. A 2023 study showed that malonyl-CoA, a molecule made during fatty acid synthesis, binds the catalytic pocket of mTOR and blocks it, linking fat production to mTORC1 activity.
Figlia is a middle author on both papers. PubMed lists the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg on both.

highlights.PRE2021: Middle author on the paper showing that G3BPs tether the TSC complex to lysosomes and restrain mTORC1.
highlights.NIC2023: Middle author on the paper identifying malonyl-CoA as an ATP-competitive mTORC1 inhibitor.

Figlia G.lab_name: German Cancer Research Center, DKFZ (Heidelberg, Germany)

Nicastro R.role: First author of a 2023 study showing that malonyl-CoA inhibits mTORC1.
Nicastro R.sub: Department of Biology · University of Fribourg, Switzerland
story: The study found that malonyl-CoA, an intermediate in making fatty acids, binds directly to the catalytic pocket of mTOR and competes with ATP, so it works as a natural mTORC1 inhibitor. When fatty acid synthase levels fall, malonyl-CoA rises and turns mTORC1 down, tying fat-making capacity to overall growth output. Nicastro is the first of fourteen authors, and PubMed lists the University of Fribourg.

highlights.NIC2023: First of fourteen authors on the paper identifying malonyl-CoA as an ATP-competitive mTORC1 inhibitor.

Nicastro R.lab_name: Department of Biology, University of Fribourg (Fribourg, Switzerland)

Nojima H.role: First author of a 2003 study on how raptor presents substrates to mTOR.
Nojima H.sub: Biosignal Research Center · Kobe University, Japan
story: This biochemical study showed that raptor, a partner protein of mTOR, binds mTOR targets such as p70 S6 kinase and 4E-BP1 through short sequences called TOS motifs. That makes raptor the part of mTORC1 that presents substrates to the kinase. Nojima is the first of ten authors, and PubMed lists the Biosignal Research Center at Kobe University.

highlights.NOJ2003: First of ten authors on the study showing that raptor binds mTOR substrates through their TOS motifs.

Nojima H.lab_name: Biosignal Research Center, Kobe University (Kobe, Japan)

Granholm AC.role: Last author of a 2026 study of mTOR and insulin signalling in the hippocampus in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease changes.
Granholm AC.sub: Department of Neurology · University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora, USA
story: The researchers used spatial transcriptomics and localized proteomics on human post-mortem brain tissue from people with Down syndrome and Alzheimer's disease changes. mTOR signalling was altered in particular parts of the hippocampus, and insulin signalling was altered in dentate granule neurons. The authors call the findings preliminary. Granholm is the last of fourteen authors, and PubMed lists the Department of Neurology at the University of Colorado Anschutz.

highlights.NOR2026: Last of fourteen authors on the study of mTOR and insulin pathways in the hippocampus in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease changes.

Granholm AC.lab_name: Department of Neurology, University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (Aurora, Colorado, USA)

Nordbeck AJ.role: First author of a 2026 study of mTOR and insulin signalling in the hippocampus in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease changes.
Nordbeck AJ.sub: Department of Neurosurgery · University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora, USA
story: The researchers used spatial transcriptomics and localized proteomics on human post-mortem brain tissue from people with Down syndrome and Alzheimer's disease changes. mTOR signalling was altered in particular parts of the hippocampus, and insulin signalling was altered in dentate granule neurons. The authors call the findings preliminary. Nordbeck is the first of fourteen authors, and PubMed lists the Department of Neurosurgery at the University of Colorado Anschutz.

highlights.NOR2026: First of fourteen authors on the study of mTOR and insulin pathways in the hippocampus in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease changes.

Nordbeck AJ.lab_name: Department of Neurosurgery, University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus (Aurora, Colorado, USA)

Okazaki H.role: First author of a 2013 mouse study on the circadian clock and mTOR in kidney cancer.
Okazaki H.sub: Graduate School of Pharmaceutical Sciences · Kyushu University, Fukuoka, Japan
story: In mice with kidney tumours, active mTOR and total mTOR protein rose and fell over 24 hours. The body clock set this rhythm through the ubiquitin ligase Fbxw7. Giving the mTOR inhibitor everolimus when mTOR was high improved survival, so the time of day of dosing changed the result. Okazaki is the first of ten authors, and PubMed lists Kyushu University.

highlights.OKA2013: First of ten authors on the mouse study showing that everolimus works better when given at the time of day when mTOR is high.

Okazaki H.lab_name: Departments of Pharmaceutics and Pharmaceutical Oncology, Graduate School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Kyushu University (Fukuoka, Japan)

Oki T.role: First author of a 2021 mouse study imaging mTORC1 activity in acute myeloid leukemia.
Oki T.sub: Center for Regenerative Medicine · Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, USA
story: Using fluorescent probes in the bone marrow of living mice, the study followed mTORC1 activity in leukemia cells. Activity fell as the disease advanced but was high at the moment of the best response to chemotherapy, where it was switched on rather than selected for. Blocking mTORC1 at that point killed more leukemia cells. Oki is the first of twelve authors, and PubMed lists the Center for Regenerative Medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital.

highlights.OKI2021: First of twelve authors on the mouse imaging study of mTORC1 timing in acute myeloid leukemia.

Oki T.lab_name: Center for Regenerative Medicine, Massachusetts General Hospital (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)

O'Reilly KE.role: First author of a 2006 study showing that mTOR inhibition switches on Akt signalling.
O'Reilly KE.sub: Program in Molecular Pharmacy and Chemistry · Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center, New York, USA
story: Blocking mTOR removes a feedback brake and turns up signalling through receptor tyrosine kinases, PI3K and Akt. The authors saw Akt activation in cancer cell lines and also in patient tumours treated with everolimus (RAD001), so part of the evidence comes from people. O'Reilly is the first of twelve authors, and PubMed lists Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center.

highlights.ORE2006: First of twelve authors on the study showing that mTOR inhibition activates Akt, in cell lines and in patient tumours.

O'Reilly KE.lab_name: Program in Molecular Pharmacy and Chemistry, Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center (New York, New York, USA)

Panchaud N.role: First author of a 2013 yeast study on a GAP complex that turns off TORC1 when amino acids run out.
Panchaud N.sub: Division of Biochemistry, Department of Biology · University of Fribourg, Switzerland
story: In baker's yeast, the Iml1 complex (with Npr2 and Npr3) acts as a GTPase-activating protein for the Rag-family protein Gtr1. When amino acids are missing, it switches Gtr1 off and so lowers TORC1 activity. The authors suggest the matching human proteins may help hold back tumours. Panchaud is the first of three authors, and PubMed lists the University of Fribourg.

highlights.PAN2013: First of three authors on the yeast study of the Iml1 GAP complex acting on Gtr1.

Panchaud N.lab_name: Division of Biochemistry, Department of Biology, University of Fribourg (Fribourg, Switzerland)

Park JM.role: First author of a 2023 cell study redefining how AMPK affects autophagy.
Park JM.sub: Department of Biochemistry, Molecular Biology and Biophysics · University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, USA
story: In cultured cells, AMPK turned out to restrain ULK1 and autophagy during glucose starvation or mitochondrial energy stress, the opposite of the usual textbook picture. AMPK also protected the ULK1 machinery from being broken down by caspases, so cells could restart autophagy later. Park is the first of three authors, and PubMed lists the University of Minnesota.

highlights.PAR2023: First of three authors on the cell study showing that AMPK inhibits ULK1 and autophagy under energy stress.

Park JM.lab_name: Department of Biochemistry, Molecular Biology and Biophysics, University of Minnesota (Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA)

Paul D.role: First author of a 2025 study on how mTOR briefly switches off APC/C to boost glycolysis at cell cycle entry.
Paul D.sub: Laboratory of Cancer Biology and Genetics · National Cancer Institute, Bethesda, USA
story: After a growth signal, mTOR quickly adds a phosphate to the APC/C helper protein CDH1, which partly releases it and briefly inactivates APC/C. The glycolysis enzyme PFKFB3 then builds up and glycolysis rises, until a later phosphatase restores APC/C. The pulse of glycolysis is needed for cells to enter the cell cycle. Paul is the first of thirteen authors, and PubMed lists the National Cancer Institute in Bethesda.

highlights.PAU2025: First of thirteen authors on the Nature paper on transient APC/C inactivation by mTOR.

Paul D.lab_name: Laboratory of Cancer Biology and Genetics, Center for Cancer Research, National Cancer Institute (Bethesda, Maryland, USA)

Peng M.role: First author of a 2017 study showing that SZT2 organizes the GATOR complexes that control mTORC1.
Peng M.sub: Immunology Program · Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, New York, USA
story: The study, in cells and mice, found that SZT2 pulls GATOR1 and GATOR2 together into one complex that sits on the lysosome and sets how mTORC1 responds to nutrients. Cells lacking SZT2 kept mTORC1 on even when starved, and SZT2-deficient newborn mice died. Peng is the first of three authors, and PubMed lists the Immunology Program at Memorial Sloan Kettering.

highlights.PEN2017: First of three authors on the study showing that SZT2 organizes GATOR control of mTORC1.

Peng M.lab_name: Immunology Program, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (New York, New York, USA)

Perez K.role: First author of a 2026 methods study on a cross-species platform for screening lifespan-extending drugs.
story: The team built a high-throughput platform that tests compounds for effects on lifespan in yeast, worms, flies, killifish and mice, using automated imaging and deep-learning death detection. More than 400 compounds were tested, and the results pointed to drugs that act in several species and to longevity pathways shared across them. This is a methods and screening study. Perez is the first of eleven authors, and PubMed lists EPITERNA in Épalinges, with other institutions in Switzerland also named.

highlights.PEREZ2026: First of eleven authors on the cross-species lifespan drug-screening platform.

Petit CS.role: First author of a 2013 study on folliculin and the lysosome-based activation of mTORC1.
Petit CS.sub: Department of Cell Biology · Yale University School of Medicine, New Haven, USA
story: In human cells, folliculin (FLCN, the protein behind Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome) gathers on lysosomes when amino acids are removed and binds RagA directly. FLCN is needed for amino acids to bring mTORC1 to the lysosome through the Rag proteins. Petit is the first of three authors, and PubMed lists the Department of Cell Biology at Yale. Petit is also listed on a 2012 TFEB paper in the Atlas, but that record carries no affiliation, so it is not counted here.

highlights.PET2013: First of three authors on the study of folliculin recruitment to lysosomes and Rag GTPase activation.

Petit CS.lab_name: Department of Cell Biology, Yale University School of Medicine (New Haven, Connecticut, USA)

Roczniak-Ferguson A.role: First author of a 2012 study showing that mTORC1 phosphorylates TFEB to control lysosome genes.
Roczniak-Ferguson A.sub: Department of Cell Biology · Yale University School of Medicine, New Haven, USA
story: In human cells, mTORC1 on the lysosome adds a phosphate to TFEB at serine 211, which lets 14-3-3 proteins hold TFEB in the cytoplasm. When lysosome function is blocked, TFEB loses the phosphate and moves into the nucleus, where it switches on lysosome and autophagy genes. Roczniak-Ferguson is the first of eight authors, and PubMed lists the Department of Cell Biology at Yale. A 2013 Atlas paper carries the same given name but no affiliation, so it is not counted here.

highlights.ROC2012: First of eight authors on the study showing that mTORC1 phosphorylates TFEB to control lysosome gene activity.

Roczniak-Ferguson A.lab_name: Department of Cell Biology, Yale University School of Medicine (New Haven, Connecticut, USA)

Pledger ES.role: First author of a 2026 study on translation of 5' TOP mRNAs in chronically activated human CD8+ T cells.
Pledger ES.sub: Department of Molecular and Cell Biology · University of California Berkeley, USA
story: Using ribosome profiling in human CD8+ T cells grown in the lab, the study found that 5' TOP mRNAs were translated much less during chronic activation, a model of T cell exhaustion. This happened even though mTOR activity looked high, so the repression is not explained by lower mTOR signalling. Pledger is the first of four authors, and PubMed lists the Department of Molecular and Cell Biology at UC Berkeley.

highlights.PLEDGER2026: First of four authors on the ribosome profiling study of 5' TOP mRNA repression in chronically activated CD8+ T cells.

Pledger ES.lab_name: Department of Molecular and Cell Biology, University of California Berkeley (Berkeley, California, USA)

Porstmann T.role: First author of a 2008 study showing that mTORC1 controls SREBP and lipid synthesis downstream of Akt.
Porstmann T.sub: Gene Expression Analysis Laboratory · London, UK
story: In cells and in fruit flies, Akt-driven lipid synthesis needed mTORC1. Rapamycin stopped the mature form of the transcription factor SREBP1 from building up in the nucleus and lowered its target genes. Silencing SREBP blocked Akt-driven fat synthesis and reduced cell size. Porstmann is the first of nine authors, and PubMed lists the Gene Expression Analysis Laboratory in London without naming a larger institution.

highlights.POR2008: First of nine authors on the study showing that mTORC1 regulates SREBP and lipogenesis in Akt-dependent growth.

Poulsen MM.role: First author of a 2012 randomized trial of high-dose resveratrol in obese men.
Poulsen MM.sub: Department of Endocrinology and Internal Medicine · Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark
story: In this randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 24 obese but otherwise healthy men took high-dose resveratrol or placebo for four weeks. Resveratrol did not improve insulin sensitivity, blood pressure or body composition, which does not match the promising results from rodents. Poulsen is the first of ten authors, and PubMed lists Aarhus University Hospital.

highlights.POU2013: First of ten authors on the placebo-controlled trial of resveratrol in obese men.

Poulsen MM.lab_name: Department of Endocrinology and Internal Medicine, Aarhus University Hospital (Aarhus, Denmark)

Pyo JO.role: First author of a 2013 mouse study showing that extra Atg5 raises autophagy and lifespan.
Pyo JO.sub: School of Biological Sciences/Bio-MAX Institute · Seoul National University, Korea
story: Mice engineered to carry extra copies of the autophagy gene Atg5 lived about 17 percent longer at the median. They were leaner and more sensitive to insulin, and cells from them resisted oxidative damage better. Pyo is the first of eight authors, and PubMed lists the Global Research Laboratory at Seoul National University.

highlights.PYO2013: First of eight authors on the mouse study of Atg5 overexpression and lifespan.

Pyo JO.lab_name: Global Research Laboratory, School of Biological Sciences/Bio-MAX Institute, Seoul National University (Seoul, South Korea)

Ramanathan C.role: First author of a 2018 study showing that mTOR sets the speed and strength of circadian clocks.
Ramanathan C.sub: Department of Biological Sciences · University of Memphis, USA
story: Blocking mTOR made circadian clocks run slower and flatter, and activating it made them run faster and stronger. This was seen in cultured cells, in brain (SCN) and liver tissue taken from mice, and in mice with one copy of the mTOR gene, whose activity rhythm ran longer. Ramanathan is the first of eight authors, and PubMed lists the University of Memphis.

highlights.RAM2018: First of eight authors on the study of mTOR and circadian clock period and amplitude.

Ramanathan C.lab_name: Department of Biological Sciences, University of Memphis (Memphis, Tennessee, USA)

Feng X.role: Last author of a 2026 study on SLC7A5, mTOR, autophagy and cisplatin tolerance.
Feng X.sub: State Key Laboratory of Oral Diseases · West China Hospital of Stomatology, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China
story: In a genome-wide CRISPR screen of cancer cells, blocking mTOR made cells more tolerant to cisplatin by switching on protective autophagy, the opposite of the usual view. The amino acid transporter SLC7A5 sits at the centre of this circuit, and adding leucine made SLC7A5-expressing tumour cells more sensitive to cisplatin. Feng is the last of seven authors, and PubMed lists the West China Hospital of Stomatology at Sichuan University.

highlights.RAO2026: Last of seven authors on the CRISPR screen study of SLC7A5, mTOR-autophagy signalling and cisplatin tolerance.

Feng X.lab_name: State Key Laboratory of Oral Diseases, West China Hospital of Stomatology, Sichuan University (Chengdu, Sichuan, China)

Rao P.role: First author of a 2026 study on SLC7A5, mTOR, autophagy and cisplatin tolerance.
Rao P.sub: State Key Laboratory of Oral Diseases · West China Hospital of Stomatology, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China
story: In a genome-wide CRISPR screen of cancer cells, blocking mTOR made cells more tolerant to cisplatin by switching on protective autophagy, the opposite of the usual view. Rao is the first of seven authors, and PubMed lists the West China Hospital of Stomatology at Sichuan University.

highlights.RAO2026: First of seven authors on the CRISPR screen study of SLC7A5, mTOR-autophagy signalling and cisplatin tolerance.

Rao P.lab_name: State Key Laboratory of Oral Diseases, West China Hospital of Stomatology, Sichuan University (Chengdu, Sichuan, China)

Rauch B.role: First author of a 2026 cell study on tankyrases, AMPK, mTOR and fat cell differentiation.
Rauch B.sub: Department of Medical Chemistry, Faculty of Medicine · University of Debrecen, Hungary
story: Deleting tankyrase 1 or 2 slowed the maturation of fat cells in a cell line, with less autophagy, more AMPK activity and weaker mTORC1 activity. The slow differentiation in TNKS2-knockout cells was rescued by activating autophagy or by blocking LKB1, and TNKS2 was found to add ADP-ribose to LKB1. Rauch is the first of eight authors, and PubMed lists the Department of Medical Chemistry at the University of Debrecen.

highlights.RAUCH2026: First of eight authors on the study of tankyrase-2, AMPK and mTOR in fat cell differentiation.

Rauch B.lab_name: Department of Medical Chemistry, Faculty of Medicine, University of Debrecen (Debrecen, Hungary)

Rebsamen M.role: First author of a 2015 study identifying SLC38A9 as part of the lysosomal amino acid sensing machinery for mTORC1.
Rebsamen M.sub: CeMM Research Center for Molecular Medicine · Austrian Academy of Sciences, Vienna, Austria
story: In human cells, SLC38A9, a transporter in the lysosome membrane, was found to be part of the Ragulator-Rag machinery. Cells with extra SLC38A9 resisted amino acid withdrawal, and cells without it activated mTORC1 poorly in response to amino acids. Rebsamen is the first of twenty authors, and PubMed lists CeMM in Vienna.

highlights.REB2015: First of twenty authors on the paper identifying SLC38A9 as a component of the amino acid sensing machinery controlling mTORC1.

Rebsamen M.lab_name: CeMM Research Center for Molecular Medicine of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (Vienna, Austria)

Ren Y.role: First author of a 2026 study on a gut-tumour bacterium, kynurenic acid and resistance to PD-1 blockade in gastric cancer.
Ren Y.sub: Department of General Surgery, Nanfang Hospital · Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, China
story: Using patient tissue and mouse models, the study linked the bacterium Streptococcus anginosus to resistance to PD-1 immunotherapy in gastric cancer. Its product kynurenic acid raised ITGA2 and dampened an mTOR-dependent chain that supports CD8+ T cell killing. Blocking ITGA2 restored T-cell activity in the models. Ren is the first of ten authors, and PubMed lists the Department of General Surgery at Nanfang Hospital.

highlights.REN2026: First of ten authors on the study of kynurenic acid, the ITGA2-mTOR-CTSV axis and PD-1 resistance in gastric cancer.

Ren Y.lab_name: Department of General Surgery, Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University (Guangzhou, China)

Robida-Stubbs S.role: First author of a 2012 study of TOR signalling, rapamycin and lifespan in worms through SKN-1 and DAF-16.
Robida-Stubbs S.sub: Joslin Diabetes Center · Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA
story: In the worm C. elegans, blocking TORC1 genetically extended lifespan through SKN-1/Nrf and DAF-16/FoxO. Rapamycin also extended lifespan, but only through SKN-1 and not DAF-16, probably because it also affects TORC2. Rapamycin triggered a similar protective response in mice. Robida-Stubbs is the first of eight authors, and PubMed lists the Joslin Diabetes Center and Harvard Medical School.

highlights.ROB2012: First of eight authors on the worm study of TOR, rapamycin and lifespan through SKN-1 and DAF-16.
